title: GitHub Integration Roadmap v1

items.title: GitHub Provider Trust Spine v1 — First Implementation Slice
items.why_it_matters: This is the first promoted implementation slice. It hardens the provider trust substrate before any additional API families, UX surfaces, or mutation lanes are added. Without this spine, broad GitHub surface expansion creates fake-green dashboards, silent data loss, and trust breaches. Every subsequent P0, P1, and P2 item depends on this slice unless explicitly implemented as part of it.
items.dependency_implications: No new dependencies. HMAC-SHA256 via stdlib hashlib. Constant-time comparison via hmac.compare_digest. Token bucket algorithm implementable with stdlib.
items.implementation_risk: medium — coordinating 7 trust-spine subsystems requires careful sequencing; webhook HMAC verification and constant-time comparison are non-negotiable
items.ui_ux_impact: Permission Transparency Panel, GitHub App Install Health Panel, What Can Rig Safely Do? Capability Surface, What Changed Since Last Run?, Why Is This Blocked? Governance Explainer — all become safe to render after trust spine

items.title: Complete secret scanning alert ingestion pipeline
items.why_it_matters: Secret scanning is the highest-severity security signal from GitHub. Without this pipeline, Rig Relay is blind to active credential leaks. Ingestion must include redaction to prevent secret material from entering telemetry or projections. Depends on GitHub Provider Trust Spine v1 (permission probe, rate-limit budget, content-light leak scanning) unless implemented as part of the same slice.
items.dependency_implications: No new dependencies. Existing httpx + pydantic sufficient for API ingestion.
items.implementation_risk: high — redaction must be provably correct; a single missed secret in telemetry is a breach
items.ui_ux_impact: Secret scanning triage queue UI in cockpit

items.title: Complete Dependabot alert ingestion pipeline
items.why_it_matters: Dependabot alerts are the primary supply chain security signal from GitHub. Without ingestion, Rig Relay has no dependency vulnerability posture. Normalization must handle all 10+ ecosystems and version formats. Depends on GitHub Provider Trust Spine v1 (permission probe, rate-limit budget, content-light leak scanning) unless implemented as part of the same slice.
items.dependency_implications: No new dependencies. Existing pydantic models sufficient.
items.implementation_risk: medium — ecosystem version format diversity requires careful normalization
items.ui_ux_impact: Dependabot triage queue UI in cockpit

items.title: Implement webhook event ingestion with idempotency
items.why_it_matters: Webhooks are the real-time event backbone for GitHub integration. Without idempotency, duplicate webhook deliveries cause duplicate alerts, double-processed mutations, and corrupted evidence. HMAC signature verification is non-negotiable. This is a trust-spine prerequisite and should be implemented within GitHub Provider Trust Spine v1.
items.dependency_implications: No new dependencies. HMAC-SHA256 via stdlib hashlib sufficient.
items.implementation_risk: high — idempotency bugs cause either data loss or data duplication; both are evidence corruption
items.ui_ux_impact: Webhook health status in cockpit provider panel

items.title: Implement rate-limit budget enforcement
items.why_it_matters: GitHub API rate limits are per-installation and exhaustion causes silent data loss across all ingestion paths. Without budget enforcement, one noisy query can starve all others. Graceful degradation must be designed, not accidental. This is a trust-spine prerequisite and should be implemented within GitHub Provider Trust Spine v1.
items.dependency_implications: No new dependencies. Token bucket algorithm implementable with stdlib.
items.implementation_risk: medium — rate-limit headers vary between github.com and GHE; budget partitioning across query types is non-trivial
items.ui_ux_impact: Rate-limit gauge in cockpit provider panel

items.title: Complete live permission probe for all capability families
items.why_it_matters: Rig Relay must not assume what permissions a GitHub App has — it must probe live. Permissions can be changed at any time by org admins. A stale permission cache means either rejected API calls or, worse, silently missing data. This is a trust-spine prerequisite and should be implemented within GitHub Provider Trust Spine v1.
items.dependency_implications: No new dependencies. GitHub App installation token introspection is REST API only.
items.implementation_risk: low — GitHub App permissions API is stable and well-documented
items.ui_ux_impact: Permission transparency panel in cockpit settings

items.title: GitHub App permission transparency in cockpit
items.why_it_matters: Users must see exactly what Rig Relay can and cannot do with their GitHub data. Permission transparency is a trust requirement — opaque permissions breed suspicion. This is the first thing a security reviewer will check.
items.dependency_implications: No new dependencies.
items.implementation_risk: low — projection layer already exists, this is a UI surface addition
items.ui_ux_impact: New permission transparency panel in cockpit settings

items.title: Sabotage tests for all mutation paths
items.why_it_matters: If Rig Relay can mutate GitHub (create PRs, issues, comments), every mutation path must survive adversarial sabotage testing. A single bypass of adoption-approval gates destroys the governance story.
items.dependency_implications: No new dependencies. Sabotage tests use existing test fixtures.
items.implementation_risk: high — sabotage tests require creative adversarial thinking and cover many edge cases
items.ui_ux_impact: Indirect — prevents bad UX from mutation bugs reaching users

items.title: PR pollution prevention tests
items.why_it_matters: Agent-authored PR comments must not spam, mislead, or leak internal state. A single bad PR comment erodes trust in the entire system. These tests are the last line of defense before agent comments reach real PRs.
items.dependency_implications: No new dependencies.
items.implementation_risk: medium — requires defining and testing against a comprehensive pollution taxonomy
items.ui_ux_impact: Governed PR comment preview in cockpit before agent comments are posted

items.title: Content-light leak detection tests for telemetry bundles
items.why_it_matters: Rig Relay's content-light telemetry promise is existential — if telemetry bundles leak raw file contents, secrets, tokens, or PII, the privacy doctrine is breached. These tests must prove the negative: nothing sensitive leaks. This is a trust-spine prerequisite and should be implemented within GitHub Provider Trust Spine v1.
items.dependency_implications: No new dependencies.
items.implementation_risk: high — proving a negative is hard; comprehensive leak detection requires adversarial creativity
items.ui_ux_impact: Indirect — privacy assurance is a trust signal, not a UI surface

items.title: Branch protection respect in preflight verification
items.why_it_matters: Rig Relay must never propose or execute a mutation that would be rejected by branch protection rules. Preflight verification prevents wasted agent cycles and, critically, prevents the agent from attempting to bypass protection rules.
items.dependency_implications: No new dependencies. Branch protection rules are read via REST API.
items.implementation_risk: medium — rulesets and classic branch protection have different API shapes and semantics
items.ui_ux_impact: Preflight verification results shown before agent proposes mutation

items.title: GitHub Operating Picture Dashboard
items.why_it_matters: The operating picture is the primary UI for viewing GitHub integration state. It must show repo health, alert counts, PR status, and CI health at a glance. Without it, users have to click through individual GitHub repos.
items.dependency_implications: No new dependencies.
items.implementation_risk: low — projection pipeline already exists, this is a UI composition task
items.ui_ux_impact: New operating picture dashboard in cockpit — primary user surface for GitHub integration

items.title: Repository Health Cockpit widget
items.why_it_matters: Per-repository health is the most common user question: 'is my repo healthy?' This widget surfaces alert counts, CI status, PR health, and branch protection compliance for a single repo in one card.
items.dependency_implications: No new dependencies.
items.implementation_risk: low — widget pattern is established in cockpit framework
items.ui_ux_impact: New repo health widget in cockpit dashboard

items.title: Issue to mission candidate routing
items.why_it_matters: GitHub issues are the most common work intake mechanism. Routing issues to mission candidates enables governed agent work that starts from a real user need. Without this, agents float without anchored tasks.
items.dependency_implications: No new dependencies. Ralph scanner already has candidate routing architecture.
items.implementation_risk: medium — issue-to-mission quality depends on issue content quality, which is variable
items.ui_ux_impact: Mission candidates surfaced in cockpit from GitHub issues

items.title: PR read pipeline with risk summary
items.why_it_matters: PR review is the highest-value agent assistance opportunity. A risk summary that considers changed files, diff size, author history, and CI status lets agents prioritize review attention. Without it, agents review every PR equally.
items.dependency_implications: No new dependencies.
items.implementation_risk: medium — risk scoring must be calibrated to avoid false confidence
items.ui_ux_impact: PR risk summary cards in cockpit

items.title: Code scanning triage queue UI
items.why_it_matters: Code scanning alerts are useless if they're just a list. A triage queue with priority, assignment, and governed action buttons turns alerts into work items. This is the solo-dev UX for security alert management.
items.dependency_implications: No new dependencies.
items.implementation_risk: low — triage queue UI pattern is well-established in cockpit widget system
items.ui_ux_impact: Code scanning triage queue in cockpit — primary security alert UI

items.title: Dependabot triage queue UI
items.why_it_matters: Dependabot alerts are a firehose without triage. A queue with severity-based sorting, ecosystem filtering, and governed action buttons turns dependency vulnerability noise into prioritized work.
items.dependency_implications: No new dependencies.
items.implementation_risk: low — same triage queue pattern as code scanning, different data source
items.ui_ux_impact: Dependabot triage queue in cockpit

items.title: Branch protection readability panel
items.why_it_matters: Branch protection rules are notoriously hard to understand from GitHub's UI. A readability panel that shows rules in plain language, highlights gaps, and flags conflicts makes security posture legible to non-admin users.
items.dependency_implications: No new dependencies.
items.implementation_risk: low — plain-language translation of structured rules data
items.ui_ux_impact: Branch protection readability panel in cockpit repo settings

items.title: What changed since last run? view
items.why_it_matters: Users need a differential view — what's new since the last time Rig Relay ran? New alerts, new PRs, new CI failures. Without this, every launch shows everything, creating alert fatigue and hiding what's actually new.
items.dependency_implications: No new dependencies. Coordination store already exists.
items.implementation_risk: low — diff computation against stored checkpoint state
items.ui_ux_impact: New 'What changed?' panel in cockpit dashboard top section

items.title: What can Rig safely do? capability surface
items.why_it_matters: Users must know what Rig Relay is capable of and permitted to do with their GitHub data. A capability surface that shows 'can read PRs? yes, can create PRs? no' builds trust and prevents surprise actions.
items.dependency_implications: No new dependencies.
items.implementation_risk: low — capability enumeration already exists, this is a projection
items.ui_ux_impact: Capability surface panel in cockpit — visible on first launch and settings

items.title: Solo maintainer mode (simplified UI)
items.why_it_matters: Solo maintainers don't need team features — they need simple, fast triage with clear action buttons. A simplified UI mode removes noise and focuses on what matters: what's broken, what's vulnerable, what needs attention.
items.dependency_implications: No new dependencies.
items.implementation_risk: low — UI mode toggle with reduced widget set
items.ui_ux_impact: Simplified cockpit layout for solo maintainers

items.title: Multi-repo portfolio view
items.why_it_matters: Teams with multiple repos need a portfolio-level view that aggregates health, alerts, and activity across repos. Without this, users must manually click through each repo, losing the forest for the trees.
items.dependency_implications: No new dependencies. Aggregation built on existing projection pipeline.
items.implementation_risk: medium — cross-repo aggregation edge cases (rate limits, different permission levels per repo)
items.ui_ux_impact: Multi-repo portfolio dashboard in cockpit

items.title: PR review packet pipeline
items.why_it_matters: Teams waste time context-switching between PRs. A review packet that bundles PR diff, CI status, CodeQL findings, and risk summary into one artifact lets reviewers make decisions faster.
items.dependency_implications: No new dependencies.
items.implementation_risk: medium — packet assembly requires coordinating multiple API calls within rate limits
items.ui_ux_impact: PR review packet cards in cockpit

items.title: Actions failure cockpit
items.why_it_matters: CI failures are the most common operational pain. An Actions failure cockpit that shows failed workflows, correlates them with recent commits/PRs, and suggests investigation paths turns red builds into actionable work.
items.dependency_implications: No new dependencies.
items.implementation_risk: low — workflow run data is straightforward to project
items.ui_ux_impact: Actions failure panel in cockpit

items.title: Release readiness panel
items.why_it_matters: Release decisions are currently made with tribal knowledge and manual checks. A release readiness panel that shows open alerts, failing CI, and branch protection status gives teams a data-driven go/no-go signal.
items.dependency_implications: No new dependencies.
items.implementation_risk: low — aggregation of existing health signals
items.ui_ux_impact: Release readiness panel in cockpit

items.title: Team activity feed
items.why_it_matters: Teams need awareness of what's happening: who opened a PR, who merged, what alerts were triaged. An activity feed collates GitHub events into a chronological team awareness stream.
items.dependency_implications: No new dependencies.
items.implementation_risk: low — event collation from existing ingestion pipelines
items.ui_ux_impact: Team activity feed in cockpit

items.title: Startup/simple mode UI
items.why_it_matters: Startups don't need enterprise features — they need fast setup, opinionated defaults, and clear next actions. A simple mode reduces cognitive load and gets teams productive in minutes.
items.dependency_implications: No new dependencies.
items.implementation_risk: low — UI mode toggle with opinionated default widget layout
items.ui_ux_impact: Simplified startup/team mode cockpit layout

items.title: PR comment to agent response queue (governed)
items.why_it_matters: When someone comments on a PR asking the agent to do something ('fix this lint error'), the agent should respond — but only through governed channels. This queue routes PR comments to agent response with full adoption-approval gating.
items.dependency_implications: No new dependencies.
items.implementation_risk: high — governed agent comments on real PRs is the highest-stakes mutation path
items.ui_ux_impact: PR comment response queue in cockpit

items.title: Secret scanning triage queue UI
items.why_it_matters: Secret scanning alerts are high-severity but often false positives (test credentials). A triage queue that shows redacted secret metadata, validation status, and governed action buttons lets users prioritize real leaks.
items.dependency_implications: No new dependencies.
items.implementation_risk: medium — redaction must be provably correct before any UI rendering
items.ui_ux_impact: Secret scanning triage queue in cockpit

items.title: PostgreSQL adapter implementation (GitHub integration portion)
items.why_it_matters: Enterprise deployments need PostgreSQL-backed evidence stores for durability, replication, and compliance. The GitHub integration code must work identically whether the backing store is local JSONL or PostgreSQL. This is the enterprise procurement table-stakes requirement.
items.dependency_implications: New dependency: asyncpg or psycopg (async PostgreSQL driver). Justification: PostgreSQL adapter is enterprise table-stakes for durability and compliance. No suitable stdlib alternative exists.
items.implementation_risk: high — store abstraction must maintain perfect equivalence between JSONL and PostgreSQL backends
items.ui_ux_impact: No direct UI impact — backend swap is transparent to cockpit

items.title: Enterprise admin panel
items.why_it_matters: Enterprise admins need organization-wide controls: which orgs are connected, what permissions are granted, who can approve mutations, audit log access. Without this panel, enterprise deployment is administratively blind.
items.dependency_implications: No new dependencies.
items.implementation_risk: medium — admin panel requires multi-org state management and role-based access
items.ui_ux_impact: Enterprise admin panel in cockpit — separate from regular settings

items.title: Multi-org portfolio analytics
items.why_it_matters: Enterprises with multiple GitHub organizations need cross-org analytics: which org has the most open alerts? Which has the worst CI health? Cross-org aggregation is the primary enterprise procurement question.
items.dependency_implications: No new dependencies. Aggregation layer already exists in analytics subsystem.
items.implementation_risk: medium — cross-org aggregation must respect data residency boundaries and rate limits
items.ui_ux_impact: Multi-org analytics dashboard in cockpit

items.title: Organization audit log ingestion
items.why_it_matters: GitHub Enterprise audit logs are required for SOC 2, ISO 27001, and FedRAMP compliance. Ingesting and normalizing audit log events lets Rig Relay serve as a compliance evidence source for enterprise security reviews.
items.dependency_implications: No new dependencies. Audit log ingestion via existing REST API client.
items.implementation_risk: high — audit log event volume is massive at enterprise scale; requires careful ingestion batching
items.ui_ux_impact: Audit log viewer in enterprise admin panel

items.title: SSO/SAML/SCIM integration planning
items.why_it_matters: Enterprise procurement requires SSO integration. Rig Relay must understand GitHub organization SSO/SAML configurations to correctly assess permission boundaries and not violate data residency constraints imposed by SAML enforcement.
items.dependency_implications: No new dependencies for planning phase. SSO implementation itself may require SAML library — deferred to P3 implementation.
items.implementation_risk: medium — SSO/SAML configuration shapes vary significantly across enterprise setups
items.ui_ux_impact: SSO configuration awareness in enterprise admin panel

items.title: Enterprise procurement evidence pack
items.why_it_matters: Enterprise procurement requires evidence: architecture diagrams, security review docs, compliance mappings, data flow diagrams. This evidence pack gives procurement teams everything they need to evaluate Rig Relay for enterprise GitHub integration.
items.dependency_implications: No new dependencies.
items.implementation_risk: low — evidence pack is documentation aggregation, not new code
items.ui_ux_impact: No direct UI impact — pack is a downloadable artifact

items.title: Fleet-wide policy engine across orgs
items.why_it_matters: Massive organizations with 100+ repos across multiple orgs need fleet-wide policies: 'all repos must have branch protection on main', 'all repos must have secret scanning enabled'. A fleet policy engine enforces organizational standards at scale.
items.dependency_implications: No new dependencies. Policy evaluation built on existing capability probes.
items.implementation_risk: high — fleet-wide policy evaluation requires efficient parallel probing across 100+ repos
items.ui_ux_impact: Fleet policy dashboard in enterprise admin panel

items.title: Massive-org analytics with materialized views
items.why_it_matters: Organizations with 500+ repos generate too much raw data for real-time analytics. Materialized views provide sub-second query performance for cross-org dashboards without hammering GitHub's API. This is the scale-up path for very large enterprises.
items.dependency_implications: No new dependencies. DuckDB already supports materialized views natively.
items.implementation_risk: medium — materialized view refresh strategies must balance freshness against resource usage
items.ui_ux_impact: Faster dashboard loading for massive-org users

items.title: Hosted/team deployment mode
items.why_it_matters: Teams don't want to run Rig Relay locally on every developer machine. A hosted deployment mode (single instance serving a team via WebSocket) reduces operational burden and enables shared state across the team.
items.dependency_implications: No new dependencies. WebSocket multi-client already supported by websockets library.
items.implementation_risk: high — multi-tenant state management, auth, and rate-limit sharing across team members
items.ui_ux_impact: Team deployment mode toggle in cockpit settings

items.title: Cross-org rate-limit budgeting
items.why_it_matters: Massive organizations with multiple GitHub orgs need rate-limit budgeting that fairly allocates API calls across orgs. Without cross-org budgeting, one busy org starves others of API access, causing silent data gaps.
items.dependency_implications: No new dependencies. Builds on P0 rate-limit budget infrastructure.
items.implementation_risk: medium — cross-org budgeting requires global rate-limit visibility and coordination
items.ui_ux_impact: Cross-org rate-limit dashboard in enterprise admin panel

items.title: Public static-site differentiation (trust center, evidence graph)
items.why_it_matters: Public trust requires public evidence. A static site that renders Rig Relay's evidence graph, competitive differentiation, and trust center content builds ecosystem credibility. This is the top-of-funnel for community adoption.
items.dependency_implications: No new dependencies. Existing Jinja2 + static render pipeline sufficient.
items.implementation_risk: low — static site rendering pipeline already exists
items.ui_ux_impact: Enhanced public documentation site with trust center and evidence graph

items.title: Copilot/workspace-adjacent workflow integration
items.why_it_matters: Rig Relay's governed agent workflow should coexist with Copilot's coding assistance. Users should be able to use Copilot for code completion and Rig Relay for governed security review — not be forced to choose one.
items.dependency_implications: No new dependencies. Coexistence is behavioral, not API integration.
items.implementation_risk: low — coexistence is about not conflicting, not deep integration
items.ui_ux_impact: Documentation and guidance on using Rig Relay alongside Copilot

items.title: Community extension API for GitHub integrations
items.why_it_matters: Ecosystem moat comes from third-party extensions. A community extension API that lets others build GitHub-integrated widgets, scanners, and projections creates network effects that competitors can't replicate.
items.dependency_implications: No new dependencies. Extension loading via existing plugin architecture.
items.implementation_risk: medium — API design must balance extensibility with governance (extensions can't bypass gating)
items.ui_ux_impact: Community extensions marketplace in cockpit

items.title: Ecosystem benchmark suite
items.why_it_matters: Competitive positioning requires data. A benchmark suite that compares Rig Relay's GitHub integration against competitors on latency, accuracy, coverage, and governance creates procurement collateral that competitors can't match with marketing alone.
items.dependency_implications: No new dependencies. Benchmark harness already exists for local inference.
items.implementation_risk: low — benchmark infrastructure already exists, this is a new benchmark suite
items.ui_ux_impact: Benchmark results published on public static site

do_not_overrun_guards: Do not implement all 25 UX surfaces in one slice — first safe cockpit surfaces after trust spine are: Permission Transparency Panel, GitHub App Install Health Panel, What Can Rig Safely Do? Capability Surface, What Changed Since Last Run?, Why Is This Blocked? Governance Explainer, and Code Scanning Triage Queue (if code-scanning pipeline is mature and content-light scan passes).
Do not add secret scanning, Dependabot, Actions logs, or PR comment workflows before content-light leak scanning and permission probes exist.
Do not implement remote mutation features before dry-run/rehearsal, approval receipts, branch protection preflight, and no-surprise mutation tests exist.
Do not wire GitHub data directly into cockpit widgets without a projection contract and content-light scan.
Do not add Postgres adapter work inside GitHub Provider Trust Spine v1 unless only schema contracts are touched.
Defer broad portfolio/admin surfaces until Postgres projection spine exists.
Defer Actions logs and artifacts UI until redaction/leak scanning is proven.
Defer PR comment response queue until no-unreviewed-generated-comments tests exist.

content_light.principle: This roadmap contains only planning metadata: item titles, priorities, risk assessments, and subsystem references. No source code, secrets, credentials, or implementation details are included. All items reference public subsystems documented in AGENTS.md.
content_light.redaction_note: No redactions applied — all content is planning metadata for publicly documented subsystems.
